analysis:
The PR changes documentation only: docs/developer/test.md (a new 'Provider authorization guidance' section at head lines 17-28, plus the surrounding unchanged test-guide text) and docs/provider/attestation.md (a date bump and one new paragraph at head line 141-142). It changes no code, keys, endpoints or authorization logic.

Security-relevant content in the attestation.md paragraph: it says that when status/doctor report App Attest authorization but MDM-removal readiness is stale, the operator should keep profiles installed and wait for a fresh coordinator decision. It also says the serving lease may stay valid after removal readiness goes stale. This is consistent with the existing text requiring a coordinator decision received within 10 seconds, a current daemon snapshot and unexpired authorization, and that a local state-file rewrite cannot extend readiness. That is conservative guidance and does not weaken T-053 (stale authorization), T-057 (premature MDM removal) or T-052. The new paragraph references ProviderAuthorizationReadiness.swift (`summary`) and ProviderAuthorizationReadinessTests. Neither implementation was supplied, so I cannot verify that the described behavior matches the code. This is a documentation-accuracy question, not a security finding. The test docs state the tests use fixed snapshots and do not establish native App Attest acceptance, which avoids overclaiming (T-056/T-058).

The other test.md text appears unchanged from base and was reviewed only as context. It describes local synthetic tests, and nothing in it introduces new attack surface. No threat-model entries need updating from this change. A later pass should confirm ProviderAuthorizationReadiness's freshness windows (10 seconds, lease expiry) against the documented claims if code from the same PR is supplied elsewhere.
